violations.text: Cheeses and Cut Watermelon were observed held at 43 and 44 degrees Fahrenheit. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Food items were moved to colder refrigeration at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/30/2026

Fruit items prepped and packaged in the food establishment are lacking labels. Food packaged in a food establishment must be labeled with the common name of the food, a list of ingredients, the quantity of the contents, and the business name/address. New Violation. Correct By: 06/30/2026

Food items in the walk-in cooler and freezers were observed stored on pallets or floor racks less than 6 inches above the floor. Food must be stored at least 6 inches above the floor. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 06/30/2026

The walk-in cooler was observed in need of repair/adjustment: - The walk-in cooler was observed holding an ambient temperature of 47 degrees Fahrenheit - A buildup of ice was observed covering the back of the walk-in condenser unit - The walk-in cooler door was observed to be lacking gaskets/seals Use of the walk-in cooler for storage of Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) Foods until service/repaired and maintaining proper ambient temperature of 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below. Call made for service. New Violation. Correct By: 06/30/2026

Wood is used in the construction of floor pallets in the walk-in cooler and for the hand sink cabinet in the kitchen area. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other food soiling or that require frequent cleaning must be constructed of a nonabsorbent and smooth material. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 06/30/2026
The door to the rest room is not self-closing. Self-closing mechanism is to be added to the door. New Violation. Correct By: 07/14/2026

Food items in the walk-in cooler and freezers were observed stored on pallets or floor racks less than 6 inches above the floor. Food must be stored at least 6 inches above the floor. New Violation. Correct By: 06/19/2025

The establishment is using a special process of jarring/preserving jams with added vegetables (Hot Pepper Jam). The product was voluntarily disposed of at the time of inspection. For jarring of vegetable items or items containing vegetables, the establishment must get all recipes approved from a process authority and obtain approval from the RIDOH-Center for Food Protection prior to selling the above mentioned products. New Violation. Correct By: 04/19/2024

The establishment is using a special process of jarring/preserving jams, pickles, and relish without approval from a process authority and the RIDOH. The jarred jams, relish, and pickle products were removed from the retail sales floor at the time of inspection. Pickle and Relish items were voluntarily disposed of and Jams were placed under embargo at the time of inspection. The establishment must get all recipes approved from a process authority and obtain approval from the RIDOH-Center for Food Protection prior to selling the above mentioned products. See Embargo New Violation. Correct By: 04/18/2024
